title: Fizzer Order
primary_metric: packaging material cost per Mini Fizzer bath bomb actually delivered (usable capacity, not raw geometric volume), in USD

options.A: Approve The Peak Box -- a square-pyramid cardstock box, tied shut at the peak
options.B: Approve The Twist Cone -- a cardstock cone, twisted shut at the point

_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC §4

deliverables.text: A dimensioned diagram (net) of each container option, drawn to scale with every face and dimension labeled, plus a surface-area comparison table showing total square inches of cardstock each option's net uses.
A capacity table: interior volume, in cubic inches, of the Peak Box and the Twist Cone.
A usable-capacity table: single Mini Fizzer sphere volume, the real packing figure applied to each container's interior volume, and the whole number of Mini Fizzers each shape can actually hold.
A material-cost-per-Mini-Fizzer-delivered comparison, combining D1's material cost with D3's usable count for each option.
A shipping-carton footprint estimate: how many of each box fit in one carton layer in a simple grid, and what percent of that layer's floor area each shape's footprint covers.

appendices.title: The Mini Fizzer: Product Spec Sheet

balance.argument_a: The Peak Box is the cheaper single container by raw material: 26.17 sq in of cardstock at $0.00089797/sq in is $0.02350/box, versus $0.02378/box for the Twist Cone. It also ships far more densely: a simple grid fits 16 Peak Boxes in one 12x12in carton layer (75.1% of the floor covered) against only 9 Twist Cones (50.3% of the floor covered) -- almost twice as many boxes per carton, which matters more than the per-box price once freight is added on top.
balance.argument_b: The Twist Cone loses on raw box price but wins on the number that the buyer actually cares about: dollars per Mini Fizzer delivered. The cone's larger interior volume (8.85 cu in vs. 7.89 cu in) holds a whole Mini Fizzer more than the Peak Box once the real 64% loose-packing figure is applied (10 fizzers vs. 9), which drops its cost-per-fizzer below the Peak Box's despite costing slightly more material per box.
balance.margin_basis: Cost per Mini Fizzer delivered = (net surface area x price per sq in) / (floor(interior volume x 0.64 / single-fizzer volume)), compared between the Peak Box and Twist Cone using Appendix B, C, D figures.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: The real 64% random loose-packing figure applies equally to the Peak Box and the tapering Twist Cone
Odalys's mold shop can only tool one shape for the season, with no mid-season change

sensitivity_note: The D4 margin (8.96%) is sensitive to MA1 -- if the Twist Cone's real packing efficiency runs meaningfully below the Peak Box's due to its taper, Option A could win instead. See FACILITATOR.md.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: MA1 (Appendix E): the true random-packing fraction for spheres settling inside a tapering cone is knowable in principle via a real production trial, but no such public figure exists. This case uses the closest public analogue -- the boxy-shape 64% figure (S3, random close packing) -- applied identically to both container shapes as a documented, disclosed estimate, not a citation for the cone-specific value. Tier 2 probe 5 (a -50% flex, a much larger swing than any plausible real-world taper penalty) pushes the margin close to SPEC section 2's 20% cap without flipping the D4 winner; see FACILITATOR.md's sensitivity note for the range where a genuine flip becomes plausible.

cohort_bands.note: Full room: Anchors 2-3 run as written; the room splits into a 'cheaper box' faction and a 'cheaper per fizzer' faction before Data Deep Dive forces everyone to actually run D3 and D4.
Compressed: Anchors 2-3 combine into one pass; D1/D2's diagrams and tables are worked as one shared example (one option) instead of every Hero building both independently.
1:1/pair: no cold-call vote at Anchor 1 -- it becomes a stated initial position instead, and the guide plays devil's advocate directly, arguing whichever side the Hero didn't pick.
